titulo: Effectiveness of Simulation-Based Training Versus Traditional Lecturing for Outbreak Investigation Among Medical Students: A Randomized Controlled Trial
tituloEs: Simulación clínica supera a la clase magistral en formación para investigación de brotes
revista: Journal of medical education and curricular development
resumenOriginal:
Introduction: Training in outbreak investigation is essential for public health readiness. This study examines how simulation-based training improves medical students' outbreak investigation skills compared to conventional lecture techniques.

Methods: We conducted a Randomized Controlled Trial (RCT) at Combined Military Hospital (CMH) Lahore Medical College over an eleven-month period. Participants were recruited from 4th-year MBBS students without any prior outbreak investigation training. Participants were randomized to control (lecture) (n = 45) and intervention (simulation) (n = 42) groups. Simulation-based training involving a Cholera outbreak scenario was compared to traditional lecture-based teaching. Pre and post-intervention assessments were used to measure knowledge, skills, and attitudes. Statistical analyses included t-tests and descriptive statistics.

Results: Simulation-based training resulted in a significantly greater improvement in knowledge and skills compared to the control group (p < 0.001). No statistically significant improvement in attitudes was observed (p = 0.068 within simulation group; p = 0.866 between groups).

Discussion: Simulation-based training was associated with greater improvement in knowledge and skills than traditional lecture-based teaching, while no significant difference was observed in attitudes. Although both groups showed increases in scores, simulation-based training was associated with greater improvement in knowledge and skills related to outbreak investigation. The outcomes specify that in order to achieve complex learning requirements, medical education needs a variety of scholastic approaches.

Conclusion: Simulation-based training was associated with greater improvement in knowledge and skills compared to traditional teaching. To augment educational outcomes and qualify aspiring healthcare professionals for real-world challenges, preceptors should think about incorporating simulation-based training into their curriculum.

tips.texto: Reserven simulación para destrezas de alta complejidad como investigación epidemiológica o diagnóstico diferencial amplio, donde la clase magistral muestra limitaciones demostrables.
Midan conocimientos y habilidades antes y después de cada método docente. Sin medición objetiva, la percepción de mejora puede ser engañosa.
La simulación no modificó actitudes significativamente. Para cambio actitudinal, consideren role-playing prolongado, reflexión guiada o mentoría longitudinal.
Usen casos de brotes reales adaptados (cólera, sarampión, COVID-19). El realismo del escenario potencia la transferencia de aprendizaje al entorno clínico.
Combinen clase magistral para fundamentos teóricos y simulación para integración práctica. Ningún método único satisface todos los objetivos de aprendizaje complejo.

sintesis: Un ensayo controlado aleatorizado con 87 estudiantes de medicina comparó simulación basada en un brote de cólera versus clase magistral. La simulación se asoció con mayor mejora en conocimientos y habilidades (p<0.001), sin diferencia en actitudes.
aplicacionDocente: Integren simulaciones de casos epidemiológicos en módulos de salud pública o medicina preventiva. Inicien con clase magistral breve sobre fundamentos del brote, luego dividan estudiantes en equipos que investiguen un escenario simulado con datos reales. Evalúen conocimientos antes y después para documentar impacto.
disenoEstudio: Ensayo controlado aleatorizado en 87 estudiantes de cuarto año sin entrenamiento previo
fraseInfografia: Simulación clínica triplica el aprendizaje de investigación de brotes versus clase magistral
advertencia: Estudio en un solo centro con escenario único (cólera), lo que limita la generalización a otros contextos epidemiológicos o instituciones.
